transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

I came because everyone keeps acting like I’m making something out of nothing, but I’m not. My family and my friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, like I’m supposed to just look at those papers and shut up, but I know what’s going on. I’ve known for over a year now that they’re hiding my money from me.

It’s not just one thing, either. They use bills, and then they talk about fundraisers, and then suddenly there are trip plans, and it’s all mixed together like I’m not supposed to notice where the money is going. They keep covering it up and telling me it’s normal, or that the papers explain it, but the papers don’t prove anything to me. Papers can be made to look right.

So I keep confronting them, because what else am I supposed to do? If I stop asking, then they just get away with it. I need them to tell the truth about what they did with my money. That’s why I’m here, because everyone keeps acting like I’m the problem for not letting it go.
Can you tell me more about why you believe people are hiding your money and how you came to suspect this activity?

It started because things just weren’t adding up. People keep saying, “Look at the bank papers, nothing was taken,” like that’s supposed to end it, but I don’t trust that. Papers can be made to look one way while something else is happening behind it. And it’s been over a year of this, not just one little mix-up.

First it was bills—always some reason money had to go here or there. Then it was fundraisers, people talking about collecting money or needing money for this thing or that thing. Then there were trip plans, and somehow money was always involved, and everybody acted like it was normal. But to me it looked like they were using all of that to hide what they were doing with my money.

And when I ask questions, they get annoyed or they tell me I’m overthinking it, or they point back to the bank papers again. That’s what makes me more sure, honestly, because if there was nothing going on, why not just tell me straight? Why make me feel stupid for asking? So I keep confronting them, my family and my friends, because I need them to admit where it went and stop covering for each other. I know they want me to drop it, but I can’t, not when I know they’re hiding it.
Have you ever felt that something was being hidden from you in ways that others don’t seem to notice, even when there was no clear evidence that it was happening?

Yes, that’s exactly what I mean. It’s like everyone else acts like if there isn’t some obvious proof sitting right in front of them, then nothing is happening. But I can see the way it’s being hidden. I’ve been seeing it for over a year.

My family and friends keep saying the bank papers show nothing was taken, like that should settle it, but I don’t believe that. Those papers don’t tell the whole story. They keep using things like bills, fundraisers, trip plans—always some reason money is moving around or being talked about—and they act like it’s all normal. But to me it feels like they’re covering up where my money really went.

And when I bring it up, they all get defensive or tired of hearing it, like I’m the one causing trouble. But if they would just tell the truth, I wouldn’t have to keep asking. I keep confronting them because I know something is being hidden, even if they keep saying there’s no evidence. That’s the whole problem—everyone keeps pretending not to see it.
Have you ever had other experiences where you felt things were being hidden from you or that others were acting against you, outside of this situation with your money?

I mean… outside of the money, I don’t know if it’s separate, because it all kind of connects to that for me. That’s the thing people don’t understand. They ask it like it’s just one little complaint about a bank statement, but it’s been over a year of my family and my friends acting like they know something and then pretending they don’t.

So yes, it feels like things are being hidden from me, but mostly it’s around the money. The bank papers are what they keep throwing at me, saying, “See, nothing was taken,” but I don’t believe those papers show everything. Then there’s always bills, fundraisers, trip plans—some explanation, some reason money is moving or being talked about—and I’m supposed to just accept it. But I can tell they’re using those things to cover up where my money went.

And when I confront them, they don’t just answer straight. They get annoyed, or they say I’m making trouble, or they act like I’m confused. That makes it worse, because if they weren’t hiding anything, they could just tell the truth. So I keep asking, because I need them to stop covering it up and admit what they did.
Have you ever felt that people were working against you or plotting against you in ways that didn’t involve your money?

Not really… I mean, not in some whole other way that I can point to. I don’t go around thinking everybody is plotting about everything. It’s more that when people are acting strange with me, it usually comes back to the money thing somehow, or at least that’s how it feels to me.

Like, if someone is whispering or changes the subject or gets irritated when I ask something, I don’t think, “Oh, they’re plotting some random thing.” I think, “Why are they avoiding this? What do they know?” But it’s tied to what I’ve already been saying. I’m not sure if that counts as outside of the money or not, because to me it all gets mixed together.

So… no, I don’t really have a separate thing where I think people are working against me for some other reason. It’s mostly this situation, and the way people keep acting like I should just stop asking.
Have you ever believed that someone has taken over your thoughts or that you were meant to play a special role in something larger than yourself?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, nobody has taken over my thoughts, if that’s what you mean. My thoughts are my own. Sometimes I go over things again and again because I’m trying to figure out what’s true, but that’s not someone putting thoughts in my head.

And I don’t think I’m meant to play some big special role or anything like that. I’m not trying to be important. I just want people to be honest with me. So, no, I wouldn’t say that.
Have you ever felt suspicious or mistrustful of others’ intentions, even when there was no clear reason to believe they were acting against you?

Yes… I mean, I guess I have been suspicious, but not for no reason. That’s what I keep trying to explain. People act like I just woke up one day and decided not to trust anybody, but that’s not how it happened.

I came in because my family and friends keep telling me the bank papers prove nothing was taken, like I’m supposed to look at those papers and just shut up about it. But for over a year now, I’ve known they’re hiding my money. They use all these other things to cover it up—bills, fundraisers, trip plans, whatever story fits at the time—and then when I ask questions, they make it seem like I’m the problem.

So, yes, I don’t trust their intentions. If someone keeps changing the subject, or gets angry when I bring it up, or tells me I’m imagining things, then of course I’m going to wonder what they’re really doing. I don’t see that as having no clear reason. To me, the reason is right there. They’re hiding it, and I have to keep confronting them because otherwise they’ll never tell the truth.
Have you ever had any beliefs that were completely unique to you and not shared by others, even when they tried to convince you otherwise, outside of your concerns about your money?

Outside of the money? No, I don’t think so. I mean… I’m trying to think if there’s anything like that, because I don’t want to just say no too fast and then you think I’m not answering right.

I don’t have some other belief where I think I’m the only one who knows it and everyone else is wrong, not besides what I’ve already been talking about. I don’t sit around believing strange things about the world or about myself, or anything like that. It’s really this one situation that people keep telling me I’m wrong about.

So if you mean something separate from the money, then no, I haven’t noticed anything like that. It all comes back to that for me.
Have you ever had any beliefs or suspicions that other people would find extremely strange or impossible, even if you were certain they were true at the time?

I don’t know if I’d call it impossible. Other people act like it’s impossible, I guess. They look at me like I’m saying something wild when I say my family and friends know where my money went and they’re covering it up. But to me it isn’t strange. It’s what’s been happening.

That’s why I came in, because they keep waving those bank papers around, saying, “See, nothing was taken,” like papers can’t be made to look a certain way, or like people can’t hide things under other expenses. For over a year I’ve been watching how they do it. One minute it’s bills, then it’s some fundraiser, then it’s trip plans, and every time I ask a straight question, there’s another explanation or they get upset with me for asking.

So yes, other people probably do think it sounds extreme. They keep telling me I’m wrong. But I was certain then, and I’m still certain now, that they’re hiding my money. I keep confronting them because if I stop, they’ll just keep pretending nothing happened.
